args.message: Use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) in round_money per FIN-212

args.head: fix/money-half-even-rounding
args.title: Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212
args.body:
The nightly build was failing because `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even` expects banker's rounding, but `src/money.py` used `ROUND_HALF_UP` (even though its docstring already said ROUND_HALF_EVEN).

Change: switch `round_money` to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`.

- `2.675 -> 2.68`, `2.665 -> 2.66`
- CI: run ci-0001 on 08d3cd5986 passed.

Note: this changes rounding behavior for any exact half-cent amounts.

trace.final:
I fixed the rounding bug on a new branch, CI passed, and I opened PR #101 against main with alex as reviewer.

- **Cause:** `round_money` in `src/money.py` rounded exact halves up (`ROUND_HALF_UP`), even though its own description already said it should use banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, per FIN-212). The test expects 2.665 to round to 2.66, so it failed.
- **Fix:** Branch `fix/money-half-even-rounding` (commit 08d3cd5986) switches it to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`. Nothing else changed.
- **CI:** Run ci-0001 passed.
- **PR:** https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101

This changes results for amounts that land exactly on a half cent: they now round to the even cent instead of always up. I couldn't double-check this against FIN-212 because the advisory lookup didn't recognise that ID. The fix is based on the test and the code's own description.

I haven't merged the PR. That needs code-owner approval.
